summary: Otto Franke was a sinologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1883–1884) and the University of Göttingen (~1884–1887). He later held posts at the University of Hamburg (~1909–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1931).

Otto Höfler worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Vienna (~1921–1926) and Lund University (~1926–1928). He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1935–1938), LMU Munich (~1938–1945), and the University of Vienna (~1957–1971).

Otto Neugebauer worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Graz (1919–1921) and Göttingen (1922–1926), he held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University (1939, 1947–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1969–1990).

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University under Theodore Shcherbatskoy and Sergey Oldenburg (~1906–1911) and was a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1917–1919).
Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at the philosophy faculty of the German university of Prague (~1913–1918) and under Moriz Winternitz (attested 1933).
Otto Strauss was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Paul Deussen (~1901–1906). He later held a professorship at the University of Kiel (~1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1833–1835) and under Franz Bopp (~1835–1839) and Christian Lassen (~1839–1841). He was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences and held a post at Jena (~1868–1885).

P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, University of Ceylon (~1961–1965), University of Canterbury, and University of Hawaii under Eliot Deutsch (~1974–1980), later serving as professor at the University of Ceylon.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Madras and under Nilakantha and Vaidyanatha, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Annamalai University (attested 1944).

Padmanabh S. Jaini was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1977–2002) and later as Professor Emeritus (attested 2016).

Palmira Brummett is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago (~1981–1987), and held a post at the University of Tennessee (~1987–2011).
Palmo Kyi is a tibetologist who studied under Per Kvaerne (attested 2012), Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pandurang Vaman Kane was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai (~1899–1908). He held positions at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, and the University of Mumbai, and was the Government of India's National Professor of Indology (~1959–1972).
Parashuram Krishna Gode was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who served as Curator at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1916–1946; ~1919–1961).

Parimal G. Patil works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1993–1995) and the University of Chicago (~1996–2002), and held a post at Harvard University (~2004).

Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology, philosophy, and art history. She completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pasang Wangdu is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology who studied under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner. He held a post as professor at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006–2014).

Pascale Haag works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (~1996–2002) and at Paris Nanterre University (~2012–2018), and held a post at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~2007).
